name: Physician

origin.rationale: Howard and Meharry opened medical schools after emancipation. Howard’s institutional history identifies the two schools as the educators of most Black physicians in the country across much of the segregation era.

citations.title: Howard University · History of the College of Medicine
Meharry Medical College · Institutional history

origin.headline: Medical schools built access

gate.rationale: Medical schools select a class. State medical boards decide who can practice after training and examinations.

citations.title: AAMC · How medical schools review applications
Federation of State Medical Boards · Physician licensure

gate.headline: School admission and medical licensing

researchQuestion: Which hospitals admitted Black physicians to training, practice and leadership?
researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: Lawyer

origin.rationale: Howard established a law school to train lawyers to defend newly secured rights. Its graduates and faculty took part in litigation against segregation. Court decisions also opened previously segregated state graduate and professional schools to Black applicants.

citations.title: Howard University School of Law · Our history
National Park Service · Court decisions in school desegregation

origin.headline: Legal education and challenges to segregation

gate.rationale: Law schools set their own application requirements. Each jurisdiction sets the conditions for admission to its bar.

gate.headline: Law school and bar admission

researchQuestion: How did bar admission translate into clients, firm employment and judicial appointments?
researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: Engineer

origin.rationale: Howard developed degree programs in civil, electrical and mechanical engineering. Federal civil rights law later extended protections against race discrimination to federally funded education. The two labels describe different contributions to access to engineering education.

citations.title: Howard University · History of engineering and architecture
U.S. Department of Education · Education and Title VI

origin.headline: Engineering education and access protections

gate.rationale: A degree is the usual starting point for civil and electrical engineers. Employers hire graduates, and some work requires a professional license. University admissions shape access to those degrees.

citations.title: Bureau of Labor Statistics · Civil engineers
Bureau of Labor Statistics · Electrical and electronics engineers

gate.headline: Education, employers and professional licensing

researchQuestion: Which employers hired Black engineers, and who gained technical or management responsibility?
researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: Dentist

origin.rationale: Howard and Meharry established dental schools serving Black students during segregation. Their training programs gave students direct access to clinical instruction and credentials that other institutions often denied them.

citations.title: Howard University College of Dentistry · About the college
Meharry Medical College · Institutional history

origin.headline: Dental schools serving Black students

gate.rationale: Dental schools evaluate applicants for admission. State boards separately determine eligibility to practice, including education and examination requirements.

citations.title: American Dental Education Association · Admissions process

name: Pharmacist

origin.rationale: Howard began pharmacy instruction in its medical department after the Civil War. Xavier later established a pharmacy college to train Black students who faced restricted access elsewhere. Both histories document HBCUs building a route into pharmacy.

citations.title: Howard University College of Pharmacy · About the college
Xavier University of Louisiana · College of Pharmacy handbook, program history

origin.headline: Institutions that trained Black pharmacists

gate.rationale: Pharmacy schools issue admissions offers. A state board then reviews a graduate’s qualifications for licensure, including examination requirements. Pennsylvania provides one worked example.

citations.title: American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy · Cooperative admissions guidelines
Pennsylvania Department of State · Pharmacist licensure guide

gate.headline: Pharmacy education and state licensing

researchQuestion: Who obtained licenses, owned pharmacies and entered hospital pharmacy in each state?
researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: Registered nurse

origin.rationale: Tuskegee trained Black nurses through a hospital school. In Jacksonville a Methodist church mission also founded a nursing school for Black women. The Jacksonville example documents church sponsorship, but it does not establish a nationwide Black-church origin.

citations.title: Tuskegee University · Nursing student handbook, program history
UF Health Jacksonville · History of nurse training in Jacksonville

origin.headline: Training, organizing and professional access

gate.rationale: Students may qualify through bachelor’s, associate degree or diploma programs. State nursing regulators license graduates who meet their requirements and pass the examination. An account limited to university degrees would miss other qualifying routes.

citations.title: Bureau of Labor Statistics · Registered nurses
National Council of State Boards of Nursing · Licensure

gate.headline: Nurse training and state licensing

researchQuestion: Which hospitals changed admission, hiring, assignments and promotion for Black nurses?
researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: K–12 teacher

origin.era: Reconstruction and the early normal schools
origin.rationale: Today’s Alabama State and Hampton universities trained teachers for Black schools. Their normal-school programs gave aspiring teachers formal instruction that they could take back to classrooms in their communities.

citations.title: Alabama State University · History and traditions
Hampton University · Institutional history

origin.headline: Communities built teacher training

gate.rationale: Public-school teachers generally need state certification. Teacher preparation and alternative routes vary, and a school or district hires the teacher. University programs are one route.

citations.title: Bureau of Labor Statistics · Kindergarten and elementary school teachers
Bureau of Labor Statistics · Middle school teachers

gate.headline: Preparation, certification and school hiring

researchQuestion: What changed for Black teachers in hiring, pay and leadership at the individual school?

name: Professor

origin.rationale: Historically Black universities such as Fisk created places to teach and pursue scholarship while segregation restricted academic opportunities. Federal civil rights protections later applied to federally funded colleges. These histories support distinct institutional and legal routes into higher education.

citations.title: Fisk University · Institutional history
U.S. Department of Education · Education and Title VI

origin.headline: Institutions sustained Black scholarship

gate.rationale: Colleges hire faculty by discipline and institution. Academic governance standards give faculty substantial responsibility for appointments. Graduate training and hiring are distinct decisions.

citations.title: Bureau of Labor Statistics · Postsecondary teachers
American Association of University Professors · Governance and academic appointments

gate.headline: Graduate training and faculty appointments

researchQuestion: Which appointments, tenure decisions and departments widened Black faculty access?
researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: Journalist / pundit

origin.era: Black press before the Civil War through the civil rights era
origin.rationale: Black communities published newspapers well before the modern civil rights movement. Publishers, editors and readers sustained that route into reporting.

citations.title: Library of Congress · African American newspapers
Library of Congress · Press and publishing

origin.headline: Black publishers built their own press

gate.rationale: News organizations hire reporters. Foundation grants also support nonprofit newsrooms, a subset tracked by the Institute for Nonprofit News. A grant decision can affect whether a newsroom can afford a position. Editors and employers make the individual hiring decisions.

citations.title: Bureau of Labor Statistics · News analysts, reporters and journalists
Institute for Nonprofit News · INN Index report

gate.headline: Editors, publishers and newsroom hiring

researchQuestion: Who controlled paid reporting and editorial authority, and when did that change?
researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: Nonprofit executive

origin.era: Mutual aid through the civil rights movement
origin.rationale: Black communities organized mutual aid through churches and voluntary associations. Church networks later supported civil rights organizations with staff and elected leaders. The sources document organizing and leadership more directly than they establish civil rights law as the origin of nonprofit executive careers.

citations.title: National Museum of American History · Free African American communities
National Park Service · Southern Christian Leadership Conference

origin.headline: Community organizing and institution-building

gate.rationale: The nonprofit’s own board selects and oversees its chief executive. A grantmaker may support the organization financially.

citations.title: BoardSource · Board responsibilities and structures
Internal Revenue Service · Foundation grants to organizations

gate.headline: Nonprofit boards appoint executives

researchQuestion: How did community leadership become paid executive work, and who made those appointments?
researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: Elected official

origin.era: Reconstruction through the voting rights movement
origin.rationale: Black voters elected representatives during Reconstruction. In later voting rights campaigns, church networks helped organize voter registration. The classification separates the institutions that mobilized communities from the electorate that selected officeholders.

citations.title: U.S. House of Representatives · Black Americans in Congress
National Park Service · Southern Christian Leadership Conference

origin.headline: Organizing, voting and holding office

gate.rationale: Voters choose representatives in congressional, state and local elections under the rules of each office. The classification follows the final election. Nominations, eligibility rules and appointments to fill vacancies are separate stages.

citations.title: USAGov · Congressional, state and local elections
USAGov · State and local elections

gate.headline: Voters, eligibility and nomination rules

researchQuestion: Where did a legal voting right become practical access to office, and where was it reversed?
researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: Pastor

origin.rationale: Black congregations built places to worship and sustain their own ministerial leadership. The African Methodist Episcopal Church is one documented example of a denomination that created an institutional route to the pulpit.

citations.title: Pew Research Center · A brief overview of Black religious history
African Methodist Episcopal Church · The AME name

origin.headline: Congregations built ministerial institutions

gate.rationale: In the African Methodist Episcopal Church, a presiding elder recommends a pastor and a bishop makes the appointment. Pastors interviewed by Pew describe diverse congregational settings. This label covers ministry in Black churches, where appointment practices vary by denomination.

citations.title: African Methodist Episcopal Church · Church structure
Pew Research Center · Interviews with Black pastors

gate.headline: Ordination and denominational appointments

researchQuestion: How did ordination and appointments differ across denominations and for Black women?
researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: Military officer

origin.era: World War I through service integration
origin.rationale: The Army’s training camp at Fort Des Moines prepared Black officers during World War I. The armed services later integrated under federal policy. Training and commissioning remained military functions as the rules governing access changed.

citations.title: National Park Service · Officer training at Fort Des Moines
Army Center of Military History · Integration of the Armed Forces

origin.headline: Training, commissions and integration

gate.rationale: Officer candidates enter through several routes, including service academies, ROTC and officer candidate schools. The service sets training and eligibility requirements and awards the commission. College admission alone does not confer officer status.

citations.title: U.S. Army · Paths to an officer commission
U.S. Army · Officer Candidate School

gate.headline: Service selection and commissioning

researchQuestion: When did commissioning lead to assignments, promotion and command in each branch?
researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: Police officer

origin.era: Civil rights enforcement in public employment
origin.rationale: Black officers served in municipal departments before federal employment protections reached state and local government. Federal law subsequently provided a way to challenge discriminatory hiring. This label describes that opening and omits earlier barriers and locally organized recruitment.

citations.title: Miami Black Police Precinct and Courthouse Museum · Overview and history
EEOC · History of the 1970s

origin.headline: Local recruitment and employment protections

gate.rationale: State standards bodies and employing agencies screen candidates. California, for example, sets minimum selection standards for peace officers. Some sheriffs stand for election. Patrol-officer hiring is a separate process from the election of a sheriff.

citations.title: California Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training · Candidate selection
Bureau of Labor Statistics · Police and detectives

gate.headline: State standards and agency hiring

researchQuestion: Which local decisions changed hiring, assignments and promotion for Black officers?
researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: Electrician / trades

origin.rationale: Electrical workers and contractors built a joint apprenticeship system that paired paid work with technical instruction. This is a documented route into the electrician trade. These sources do not establish how accessible individual programs were to Black applicants across regions.

citations.title: Electrical Training Alliance · History of joint apprenticeship training
Bureau of Labor Statistics · Electricians

origin.headline: Apprenticeships, organizing and Black enterprise

gate.rationale: Unions and contractors sponsor apprenticeship programs, and some employers train electricians through other routes. States and localities often require a license. The trade label identifies an important training gate, with the legal permission to work determined separately.

citations.title: Bureau of Labor Statistics · Electricians
Electrical Training Alliance · History of joint apprenticeship training

gate.headline: Training sponsors, employers and licensing

researchQuestion: Who entered the local apprenticeship, received job referrals and gained paid contracts?

name: Software engineer

origin.rationale: The growth of packaged software created jobs in firms that sold code and services. Computing also grew inside research institutions and public agencies. Commercial demand is one documented route. Its weight in the history of Black software careers needs further review.

citations.title: Computer History Museum · Software and the computer industry
Computer History Museum · Trailblazers and change agents

origin.headline: Education, research and employer opportunities

gate.rationale: Employers across industries hire software developers, usually looking for technical preparation and often a degree. The market label refers to selection by employers. Large firms, small contractors and public employers make separate hiring decisions.

O*NET · Software developers

gate.headline: Technical preparation and employer hiring

researchNote: Field history is not proof of an individual hiring route.

name: Corporate executive

origin.rationale: Federal employment law gave workers a way to contest race discrimination in hiring and promotion. It helps explain a change in access to corporate careers. Establishing the origins of Black executive leadership also calls for evidence on advancement inside firms and earlier Black-owned businesses.

citations.title: EEOC · History of federal employment law
Library of Congress · African Americans in business and entrepreneurship

origin.headline: Employment protections and advancement

gate.rationale: Corporate boards manage or oversee company affairs. Officers are selected under corporate bylaws or board decisions, as Delaware law illustrates.

citations.title: Delaware Code · Directors and officers
Bureau of Labor Statistics · Top executives

gate.headline: Boards and company appointment rules

researchQuestion: Who sponsored and appointed Black executives, and what authority did those roles carry?

name: Entrepreneur

origin.rationale: Black-owned shops and firms supplied goods and services in urban business districts. The Nation of Islam later built businesses of its own, including enterprises in Chicago. These are distinct histories. Entrepreneurship among Black Americans long predates that organization.

citations.title: National Park Service · Chicago’s Black Metropolis
Encyclopedia of Chicago · Nation of Islam

origin.headline: Black enterprise across different eras

gate.rationale: Founders choose a market, raise funds and start serving customers. Registration and licensing depend on the business and its location. Customer demand is central to keeping a firm open, while access to capital and permits affects whether it can launch.

citations.title: U.S. Small Business Administration · Plan your business
U.S. Small Business Administration · Launch your business

name: Pro athlete (NFL / NBA)

origin.rationale: Pro football teams resumed signing Black athletes after an exclusionary period, and NBA teams began integrating around the same era. The market label refers to paid roster places offered by teams. League histories document racial exclusion alongside commercial demand.

National Basketball Association · League integration anniversary

origin.headline: Integration of professional football and basketball

National Basketball Players Association · Collective bargaining agreement

origin.rationale: Black-owned record labels created paid recording opportunities for Black performers. Black Swan is one documented example. The category names the commercial route into recording. Churches, community ensembles and other institutions also sustained musicians outside that market.

Library of Congress · Early African American music

Sphinx Organization · Orchestral Partners Auditions
